items.readable_text:
Content:
The cumulative distribution function (or CDF) of a continuous random variable is defined the same way as for a discrete random variable.

Content:
Given a continuous random variable [MATH: X,] the CDF is the function [MATH: F(x)] such that

Content:
[MATH: F(x) = P(X \leq x).]

Content:
If our random variable has the probability density function (or PDF) [MATH: f(x),] then we have

Content:
[MATH: F(x) = P(X \leq x) = \int_{-\infty}^x f(t) \, \textrm dt.]

Content:
Note that we use [MATH: f(t)dt] in the integrand because [MATH: x] serves as the upper limit of integration.

Content:
For example, consider the random variable [MATH: X] with the following PDF:

Content:
[MATH: {(2)/(π(1 + x^{2})),|x ∈ [0, ∞); 0,|otherwise]

Content:
Since [MATH: f(x)= 0] for all [MATH: x < 0,] we have
[MATH: F(x) = \int_{-\infty}^x 0 \, \textrm dt = 0]
if [MATH: x<0.]

Content:
To compute the CDF for [MATH: x\geq 0,] we integrate [MATH: f(x)] as follows:

Content:
[MATH: F(x)|= ∫_{− ∞}^{x}f(t)dt; = ∫_{− ∞}^{0}f(t)dt + ∫_{0}^{x}f(t)dt; = 0 + ∫_{0}^{x}(2)/(π(1 + t^{2}))dt; = (2)/(π)\arctan t|_{0}^{x}; = (2)/(π)\arctan x − (2)/(π)(0); = (2)/(π)\arctan x]

Content:
Expressing our CDF as a function defined over the entire real line, we get

Content:
[MATH: {0,|x < 0,; (2)/(π)\arctan x,|x ≥ 0.]

sections.readable_text:
Given that the random variable [MATH: X] has the probability density function
[MATH: {e^{− x},|x ≥ 0,; 0,|x < 0,]

find the cumulative distribution function [MATH: F(x).]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Since our random variable [MATH: X] has a probability distribution function [MATH: f(x)] that is strictly positive only for [MATH: x \geq 0,] the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

[MATH: {0,|x < 0,; ∫_{0}^{x}f(t)dt,|x ≥ 0.]

For the given probability density function, we have

[MATH: ∫_{0}^{x}f(t)dt|= ∫_{0}^{x}e^{− t}dt; = − e^{− t}|_{0}^{x}; = − e^{− x} + 1; = 1 − e^{− x}.]

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by

[MATH: {0,|x < 0,; 1 − e^{− x},|x ≥ 0.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Since our random variable [MATH: X] has a probability distribution function [MATH: f(x)] that involves an absolute value, the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

[MATH: {∫_{− ∞}^{x}e^{2t}dt,|x < 0,; ∫_{− ∞}^{0}e^{2t}dt + ∫_{0}^{x}e^{− 2t}dt,|x ≥ 0.]

Let's compute the integrals.

  • If [MATH: x \leq 0,] we have [MATH: ∫_{− ∞}^{x}e^{2t}dt|= (e^{2t})/(2)|_{− ∞}^{x}; = (e^{2x})/(2),] Therefore, [MATH: ∫_{− ∞}^{0}e^{2t}dt|= (e^{2x})/(2)|_{x = 0}; = (1)/(2).]

  • If [MATH: x > 0,] we have [MATH: ∫_{0}^{x}e^{− 2t}dt|= − (e^{− 2t})/(2)|_{0}^{x}; = − (e^{− 2x})/(2) + (1)/(2).] As a result, we get [MATH: ∫_{− ∞}^{0}e^{2t}dt + ∫_{0}^{x}e^{− 2t}dt|= (1)/(2) + (− (e^{− 2x})/(2) + (1)/(2)); = 1 − (e^{− 2x})/(2).]

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by

[MATH: {(e^{2x})/(2),|x < 0,; 1 − (e^{− 2x})/(2),|x ≥ 0.]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
The cumulative distribution function (or CDF) of a continuous random variable is defined the same way as for a discrete random variable.

Content:
Given a continuous random variable [MATH: X,] the CDF is the function [MATH: F(x)] such that

Content:
[MATH: F(x) = P(X \leq x).]

Content:
If our random variable has the probability density function (or PDF) [MATH: f(x),] then we have

Content:
[MATH: F(x) = P(X \leq x) = \int_{-\infty}^x f(t) \, \textrm dt.]

Content:
Note that we use [MATH: f(t)dt] in the integrand because [MATH: x] serves as the upper limit of integration.

Content:
For example, consider the random variable [MATH: X] with the following PDF:

Content:
[MATH: {(2)/(π(1 + x^{2})),|x ∈ [0, ∞); 0,|otherwise]

Content:
Since [MATH: f(x)= 0] for all [MATH: x < 0,] we have
[MATH: F(x) = \int_{-\infty}^x 0 \, \textrm dt = 0]
if [MATH: x<0.]

Content:
To compute the CDF for [MATH: x\geq 0,] we integrate [MATH: f(x)] as follows:

Content:
[MATH: F(x)|= ∫_{− ∞}^{x}f(t)dt; = ∫_{− ∞}^{0}f(t)dt + ∫_{0}^{x}f(t)dt; = 0 + ∫_{0}^{x}(2)/(π(1 + t^{2}))dt; = (2)/(π)\arctan t|_{0}^{x}; = (2)/(π)\arctan x − (2)/(π)(0); = (2)/(π)\arctan x]

Content:
Expressing our CDF as a function defined over the entire real line, we get

Content:
[MATH: {0,|x < 0,; (2)/(π)\arctan x,|x ≥ 0.]

---

Item 2 — Example: Finding a CDF Given a PDF With a Lower Bound

Example Prompt:
Given that the random variable [MATH: X] has the probability density function
[MATH: {e^{− x},|x ≥ 0,; 0,|x < 0,]

find the cumulative distribution function [MATH: F(x).]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Since our random variable [MATH: X] has a probability distribution function [MATH: f(x)] that is strictly positive only for [MATH: x \geq 0,] the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

[MATH: {0,|x < 0,; ∫_{0}^{x}f(t)dt,|x ≥ 0.]

For the given probability density function, we have

[MATH: ∫_{0}^{x}f(t)dt|= ∫_{0}^{x}e^{− t}dt; = − e^{− t}|_{0}^{x}; = − e^{− x} + 1; = 1 − e^{− x}.]

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by

[MATH: {0,|x < 0,; 1 − e^{− x},|x ≥ 0.]

Item 5 — Example: Computing a CDF Given a PDF That’s Nonzero Over All Real Numbers

Example Prompt:
Given that the random variable [MATH: X] has the probability density function
[MATH: f(x) = e^{-|2x|}, \quad x \in (-\infty, \infty),]

find the cumulative distribution function [MATH: F(x).]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Since our random variable [MATH: X] has a probability distribution function [MATH: f(x)] that involves an absolute value, the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

[MATH: {∫_{− ∞}^{x}e^{2t}dt,|x < 0,; ∫_{− ∞}^{0}e^{2t}dt + ∫_{0}^{x}e^{− 2t}dt,|x ≥ 0.]

Let's compute the integrals.

- If [MATH: x \leq 0,] we have
[MATH: ∫_{− ∞}^{x}e^{2t}dt|= (e^{2t})/(2)|_{− ∞}^{x}; = (e^{2x})/(2),]
Therefore,
[MATH: ∫_{− ∞}^{0}e^{2t}dt|= (e^{2x})/(2)|_{x = 0}; = (1)/(2).]
- If [MATH: x > 0,] we have
[MATH: ∫_{0}^{x}e^{− 2t}dt|= − (e^{− 2t})/(2)|_{0}^{x}; = − (e^{− 2x})/(2) + (1)/(2).]
As a result, we get
[MATH: ∫_{− ∞}^{0}e^{2t}dt + ∫_{0}^{x}e^{− 2t}dt|= (1)/(2) + (− (e^{− 2x})/(2) + (1)/(2)); = 1 − (e^{− 2x})/(2).]

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by

[MATH: {(e^{2x})/(2),|x < 0,; 1 − (e^{− 2x})/(2),|x ≥ 0.]

Item 8 — Tutorial: Finding a CDF Given a PDF With Lower and Upper Bounds

Content:
When a random variable [MATH: X] has a probability distribution function [MATH: f(x)] that is strictly positive on the interval [MATH: a \leq x \leq b] only, we have

Content:

- [MATH: P(X \leq x) = 1] for [MATH: x > b.]

Content:
In these cases, the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

Content:
[MATH: {0,|x < a; ∫_{a}^{x}f(t)dt,|a ≤ x ≤ b; 1,|x > b]

Since our random variable [MATH: X] has a probability distribution function [MATH: f(x)] that is strictly positive only for [MATH: 0 \leq x \leq 12,] the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by

[MATH: {0,|x < 0; (x^{2})/(144),|0 ≤ x ≤ 12; 1,|x > 12.]
